skill.name: vue-debug-guides
skill.description: Vue 3 debugging guides for runtime errors, warnings, reactivity issues, async failures, and SSR hydration problems.
skill.summary: Diagnose Vue 3 runtime, reactivity, async component, and SSR hydration issues with targeted debugging guides.
skill.author: vuejs-ai

security_audit.summary: The static findings are documentation false positives in Vue guide Markdown, not executable skill behavior. High-severity matches resolve to harmless Vue terms such as event.key, keys(), import.meta.env.DEV, and IME keystroke prose; no prompt injection or malicious intent was found.

remediation.issue: Static scanners flag many educational snippets because they mention network, file, dynamic import, and key-related APIs.
remediation.suggestion: Mark examples clearly as documentation and keep dangerous-looking APIs inside fenced examples with explanatory safety notes.

remediation.issue: Some debugging examples expose internal state to the browser window during development.
remediation.suggestion: Keep these helpers guarded by development flags and add reminders to remove them from production builds.

content.value_statement: Vue bugs often come from reactivity timing, component boundaries, async loading, or SSR hydration mismatches. This skill routes Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to targeted Vue 3 debugging guides.
actual_capabilities: Maps Vue 3 symptoms to focused reference guides for common runtime and template errors.
Explains reactivity, computed, watcher, and template ref debugging patterns.
Covers async component, Suspense, KeepAlive, and Vue Router edge cases.
Guides SSR hydration, cross-request state, and platform-specific API diagnosis.
Provides examples for TypeScript, render functions, plugins, forms, slots, and transitions.
limitations: The skill provides guidance and examples, not automated code execution or project scanning.
It focuses on Vue 3 and may not apply to older Vue 2 code without adaptation.
Examples are diagnostic patterns and should be reviewed before use in production.
It does not replace framework documentation for version-specific API changes.

use_cases.title: Resolve Runtime Vue Errors
use_cases.description: Find likely causes for warnings, undefined refs, missing components, and template expression failures.

use_cases.title: Debug SSR Hydration Problems
use_cases.description: Identify state sharing, browser-only API usage, and HTML mismatch causes in server-rendered Vue apps.

use_cases.title: Review Vue Patterns During Migration
use_cases.description: Check Composition API, script setup, dynamic components, and render function behavior during Vue 3 migration.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose A Vue Warning
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner debugging of a visible warning or runtime error.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use vue-debug-guides to explain this Vue warning. List likely causes, the best matching guide, and the first checks to make.

prompt_templates.title: Trace Reactivity Behavior
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate debugging of stale computed values, watchers, or refs.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use vue-debug-guides to debug this reactivity issue. Compare computed, watcher, ref, and template ref causes before recommending a fix.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate Async Component Failure
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced debugging of lazy loading, Suspense, KeepAlive, or router behavior.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use vue-debug-guides to analyze this async component issue. Include loading, error, Suspense, KeepAlive, and router interactions.

prompt_templates.title: Audit SSR Hydration Mismatch
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of SSR or universal rendering failures.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use vue-debug-guides to review this SSR hydration mismatch. Separate server output, client state, browser API, and cross-request risks.

output_examples.input: A computed property updates once, then stops after a conditional branch changes.
output_examples.output: The response points to conditional computed dependencies, explains skipped tracking, and suggests reading all reactive dependencies consistently.

output_examples.input: A lazy route component shows the wrong loading state under Suspense.
output_examples.output: The response compares router lazy imports, async components, Suspense ownership, and error UI behavior.

output_examples.input: An SSR page hydrates with different user data after concurrent requests.
output_examples.output: The response identifies possible cross-request state pollution and recommends per-request state factories.

best_practices: Start from the exact Vue warning or symptom, then choose the closest reference guide.
Check whether the issue is timing, reactivity tracking, component scope, or SSR environment mismatch.
Validate examples against your Vue version, build tool, and production constraints before applying them.
anti_patterns: Do not apply every example blindly without matching it to the observed symptom.
Do not treat dev-only debugging helpers as production instrumentation.
Do not mix Vue 2 and Vue 3 mental models when debugging Composition API behavior.

faq.question: Does this skill modify my Vue project?
faq.answer: No. It provides diagnostic guidance and examples for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to use during analysis.

faq.question: Which Vue versions does it target?
faq.answer: It targets Vue 3, including Composition API, script setup, Suspense, Teleport, and SSR behavior.

faq.question: Can it debug SSR hydration mismatches?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guides for hydration causes, cross-request state, browser-only APIs, and SSR lifecycle behavior.

faq.question: Does it run network or file system commands?
faq.answer: No. The package is documentation. Some examples discuss network and file APIs inside Vue application code.

faq.question: Can it help with TypeScript Vue errors?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers typed event handlers, defineProps limitations, template refs, dynamic components, and template casting.

faq.question: How should I use it with Claude Code or Codex?
faq.answer: Provide the warning, affected component, Vue version, and recent changes, then ask for the closest matching guide.
